title: An explicit joint Laplace transform for Brownian first-visit cell lengths on a circle
description:
We give a complete analytic-transform answer to Georgakopoulos's finite-particle circle first-visit cell-length question in Oberwolfach Report 23/2018, printed p. 1452. For arbitrary fixed distinct labeled seeds, equally spaced seeds, and independent uniform seeds, the full joint Laplace transform is an absolutely convergent series with coefficients reduced to finite permutation sums and deterministic integrals of explicit interval-exit kernels over cumulative physical-clock inequalities. A uniform factorial bound controls the outer series, and compact-support moment determinacy fixes the joint measure. No named density, fast algorithm, or certified inner numerical quadrature is claimed.

Earlier competing-walk painting results and classical heat-kernel, strong-Markov and moment methods are credited. A bounded primary-source audit dated October 7, 2026 did not identify a prior complete characterization of the general target law. Close historical full-text access and Zenodo registry-search limitations are disclosed; no absolute priority, exhaustive absence, or independent-discovery claim is made.

AI tools were used extensively in developing, drafting, reproducing and adversarially verifying this work. Independent AI reviews are not conventional human peer review. This preprint is unrefereed and has not undergone conventional human peer review. The support archive provides source, provenance, priority comparisons, and distinct exact finite-model and high-precision scalar diagnostics; these diagnostics are not a Brownian proof or numerical-error certificate.
